page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.32-512 is an Arm-based virtual machine configuration built on the Ampere AmpereOne processor architecture. The instance allocates 64 dedicated physical cores running at a sustained base frequency of 3.0 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, providing 64 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core. This dedicated single-thread-per-core layout ensures consistent execution times by avoiding hyperthreading contention across concurrent compute tasks.

The system is provisioned with 512.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per core ratio aligned with memory-intensive workloads. No local NVMe or bundled local disk storage is included with the instance, requiring all durable and scratch space to be attached via remote block storage volumes. Accelerators are omitted, with zero GPUs present. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address alongside standard virtual cloud network interfaces.

Featuring a high memory-to-core ratio and consistent single-threaded core execution, VM.Standard.A2.Flex.32-512 targets large-scale in-memory caching platforms, distributed relational or NoSQL database clusters, and memory-dense container deployments. On a qualitative level, Ampere-based compute offers power-efficient processing capacity, allowing dense multi-core configurations to operate with favorable resource efficiency when paired with Arm-native enterprise stacks.

The server provides balanced multi-threaded throughput and elevated memory capacity, functioning as a platform for distributed databases, large in-memory caches, big data processing, and Arm64 container orchestration.
